newsitem.title: INDONESIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - August 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - August 4.

text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Indonesian press on August 4. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

The ousted leader of the minority Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI) Megawati Sukarnoputri said she was happy with a Jakarta High Court verdict ordering a lower court to hear her case against rivals in the party.
The High Court ruled that the Central Jakarta Court should hear a case filed by Megawati challenging the holding of a party congress in June 1996 where she was replaced as PDI chief.
Leading Indonesian economist Sjahrir has reminded property developers to be cautious when chosing banks to fund their projects because many cases of problem banks could arise.
A blanket of haze has enveloped the central Kalimantan town of Palangkaraya, with its main airport closed to traffic.
A weekend raid on nightspots in East Jakarta netted, among others, several members of the armed forces for being in places out of bounds.

The South African government has officially made Portugal's ambassador to Pretoria persona-non-grata and ordered him to leave the country within 48 hours. Quoting sources in South Africa, the newspaper said the move followed leaks of a letter President Nelson Mandela wrote to Indonesia's President Suharto urging the release of East Timor resistance leader Xanana Gusmao who is serving a 20-year jail term. The letter had been mistakenly delivered to the Portuguese embassy.
